fourteen_thousand_two_hundred_origin: FOUND as an assumption, not a manufacturer spec and not a measurement. It is the hardcoded constant NOMINAL_LENS_DIAMETER_UM = 14_200.0 in /data/FMD_Data_26082026/measure_scale.py line 9, and 14200.0 in eda_size_um.py line 24. The only stated rationale is eda_methodology.html section 21.3 line 393: 'NOMINAL_LENS_DIAMETER_UM = 14 200      (soft daily contact lens; spec range 14.0 to 14.3 mm)'. So the prior EDA records 14,200 as the nominal diameter of a soft daily contact lens whose spec range is claimed to be 14.0 to 14.3 mm. That range is our own assertion with no source document (see lens_spec_origin). No received document states how 14,200 was arrived at; the recorded chain is an assumed 14.2 mm product diameter divided by a measured lens rim of 778 or 783.8 px.
lens_spec_origin: FOUND BUT INCONSISTENT. The 14.0 to 14.3 mm range is written only in our own generated artifacts: eda_methodology.html section 21.3 line 393 ('spec range 14.0 to 14.3 mm'), build_size_dashboard.py lines 120 to 121 ('Divide the nominal soft-lens diameter (14.2 mm, spec range 14.0 to 14.3) by that.'), and eda_defect_size_um.html lines 86 to 87 (same prose). It is in no received document, and it is not reflected in the current record: docs/reference/received_docs_nominals.md states the lens diameter 'is written in no received document present here' and that 14,200 'is our own figure'. The prior EDA presents the range as a known product spec and cites no source for it, and it folds the range into the stated 6 percent uncertainty. The user's guess is correct: its only home is the earlier experiment.
